output.text:
REINFORCED 40 MM DIRECT HEX WHEEL MOUNT - TWO COPIES

Use shaft_pair_direct_hex_M3_40mm_reinforced.stl for slicing or the matching STEP for editing.
Units: millimeters. Both files contain only the two shaft/hub pieces.

The printed hex replaces the brass adapter and the old 5 mm shaft neck.
The wheel mounts directly onto the new hex.

FIT DIMENSIONS
Mounting base top face to hex tip: 40.0 mm.
Overall height including mounting base thickness: 42.7 mm.
The exposed extension has a solid 12 mm-diameter central span with smooth transitions.
The original 8 mm bearing seat is retained. The bottom bore retains its previous depth.
The thickening starts above the original bearing seat; check clearance to any nearby chassis parts.
Strength improvement has not been measured by load testing.
Hex: 11.8 mm across opposite flat faces; 5.8 mm long.
Intended wheel recess: approximately 12 mm across flats and 6 mm deep.
Bottom bore: 5.6 mm diameter, retaining its original 15.366664 mm depth.
Other gearbox mounting features are retained.
Two identical pieces, approximately 10 mm apart.

HARDWARE PER WHEEL
One standard M3 hex nut, 5.5 mm across flats and 2.4 mm thick.
One M3 retaining screw; the existing 8 mm screw may be usable, subject to the check below.
The nut pocket is not sized for a tall nylon-insert locknut.
Nut dimensions reference: https://www.accu.co.uk/hexagon-nuts/766459-NUT203M3

ASSEMBLY
1. Clean the side opening and slide the M3 nut into its pocket until its hole aligns with the central screw hole.
2. Test-fit the wheel over the hex. Do not force it or use the screw to pull an excessively tight hex into place.
3. Seat the wheel against the support flange, covering the nut-loading opening.
4. Pass the M3 screw through the wheel and thread it into the captive nut. Tighten gently.

SCREW-LENGTH CHECK
For nominal full engagement through the 2.4 mm nut, the screw should project at least 4.1 mm beyond the wheel's inner screw-hole surface into its hex recess.
For an 8 mm screw, this corresponds to at most 3.9 mm between the underside of its seated head and that inner surface, including any washer.
The actual wheel thickness is unknown, so fit of the 8 mm screw has not been confirmed.
If it cannot reach fully through the nut, use a suitable longer M3 screw after checking that it will not bottom out.
The hub has 8.3 mm of screw-tip clearance measured inward from its hex tip. This clearance is separate from the wider bottom bore.

VALIDATION
The STEP reopens as two valid solids. The nominal wheel recess, nut insertion path, and resistance to nut rotation were checked geometrically.
Printed fit, retention strength, wheel clearance against the gearbox housing, and load capacity require a physical test. The wheel's overall shape was not supplied.

The direct-hex model is built. I verified that it clears a nominal 12 × 6 mm wheel recess and that a standard M3 nut can slide into the side pocket but cannot rotate once centered.

For full nut engagement, the screw needs to project about 4.1 mm through the wheel. I’ll include that check with the files, since the actual screw fit is still unconfirmed.

diff.text:
DIRECT HEX WHEEL MOUNT — TWO COPIES

Use shaft_pair_direct_hex_M3.stl for slicing or the matching STEP for editing.
Units: millimeters. Both files contain only the two shaft/hub pieces.

The printed hex replaces the brass adapter and the old 5 mm shaft neck.
The wheel mounts directly onto the new hex.

FIT DIMENSIONS
Hex: 11.8 mm across opposite flat faces; 5.8 mm long.
Intended wheel recess: approximately 12 mm across flats and 6 mm deep.
Bottom bore: 5.6 mm diameter, retaining its original 15.366664 mm depth.
Other gearbox mounting features are retained.
Two identical pieces, approximately 10 mm apart.

HARDWARE PER WHEEL
One standard M3 hex nut, 5.5 mm across flats and 2.4 mm thick.
One M3 retaining screw; the existing 8 mm screw may be usable, subject to the check below.
The nut pocket is not sized for a tall nylon-insert locknut.
Nut dimensions reference: https://www.accu.co.uk/hexagon-nuts/766459-NUT203M3

ASSEMBLY
1. Clean the side opening and slide the M3 nut into its pocket until its hole aligns with the central screw hole.
2. Test-fit the wheel over the hex. Do not force it or use the screw to pull an excessively tight hex into place.
3. Seat the wheel against the support flange, covering the nut-loading opening.
4. Pass the M3 screw through the wheel and thread it into the captive nut. Tighten gently.

SCREW-LENGTH CHECK
For nominal full engagement through the 2.4 mm nut, the screw should project at least 4.1 mm beyond the wheel's inner screw-hole surface into its hex recess.
For an 8 mm screw, this corresponds to at most 3.9 mm between the underside of its seated head and that inner surface, including any washer.
The actual wheel thickness is unknown, so fit of the 8 mm screw has not been confirmed.
If it cannot reach fully through the nut, use a suitable longer M3 screw after checking that it will not bottom out.
The hub has 8.3 mm of screw-tip clearance measured inward from its hex tip. This clearance is separate from the wider bottom bore.

VALIDATION
The STEP reopens as two valid solids. The nominal wheel recess, nut insertion path, and resistance to nut rotation were checked geometrically.
Printed fit, retention strength, wheel clearance against the gearbox housing, and load capacity require a physical test. The wheel's overall shape was not supplied.

items.text:
For drive wheels, **the shorter shaft and rounded junction should help, but a 5 mm PLA shaft can still fail under wheel loads**. PLA is relatively brittle, especially under impacts. [Prusa’s PLA guide](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/pla_2062)

For your next test, I’d use the reinforced version with:

- **The shaft horizontal, with supports**, to improve resistance to bending across layer lines. The supported surface may need cleanup for the adapter.
- **6 walls with a 0.4 mm nozzle**, and solid infill through the shaft and junction. Extra walls generally contribute more to strength than increasing infill alone. [Prusa’s guidance](https://help.prusa3d.com/article/infill_42)
- The brass adapter close to the rounded shoulder, with its set screw snug against the flat—avoid crushing the PLA.

**Are the wheels supported by a separate bearing, or hanging directly off these shafts?** If they’re unsupported, the junction carries the robot’s weight and wheel impacts as well as drive torque; adding bearing support would address that bending load.
